subject: first attempts with tidyverse and pipes

messages.author: bbea236abe87368e
messages.subject: first attempts with tidyverse and pipes
parts:
Hi all, 

I am trying to make the leap to tidy data and using pipes, with the hope that both my data and my code will therefore be more accessible to others. I’ve run into an error that has me a bit stumped, and would appreciate your insights on where my novice understanding of these tools is going wrong!

I’ve written a function to convert my “messy” dataframe into a tidier form. Written this way, the function works:
---
tidyfy_transect_data <- function(df, first.species, last.species){

  first.species.index <- which(names(df)==first.species)
  last.species.index <- which(names(df)==last.species)
  df %>% 
    select(first.species.index:last.species.index) %>%
    names()
    
  gather(df, key='veg.species', value='veg.present’)

}

# with the call
tidyfy_transect_data(transect.binary.2016, 'ACHMIL', 'ZELTRI’)
---

But set up as one whole series of pipes (which I would prefer as I would like to do more things with the output of the gather() call), the function does not work, and results in an error: "there is no applicable method for ‘gather_’ applied to an object of class ‘character’.” 

---
tidyfy_transect_data <- function(df, first.species, last.species){

  first.species.index <- which(names(df)==first.species)
  last.species.index <- which(names(df)==last.species)
  df %>% 
    select(first.species.index:last.species.index) %>%
    names() %>%
    gather(key='veg.species', value='veg.present’)

}
# with the call
tidyfy_transect_data(transect.binary.2016, 'ACHMIL', 'ZELTRI')
—

What about these two versions is different? Also, is there a better way to pass column names into a function than my silly work-around in the first two lines? I have attached a csv of the input dataframe. Thank you for your ideas!

messages.author: 47ca46208a81ec5e
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: first attempts with tidyverse and pipes
parts:
Hi Chhaya,

Welcome to tidyr!

The difference between your two functions arises because the pipe doesn’t do assignment. As you know, the pipe takes the result of the operation on its left and passes it as the first argument to the function on its right. But as in R more generally, the result of an operation is lost unless it is assigned to a variable.

So in your first function, you take the ‘df’ object (which was passed as an argument to your function), perform a select() on it to choose certain columns, and then call the names() function on the data frame with only some of its columns selected. But the result of this operation is lost after the pipeline ends because its result wasn’t assigned to a new variable (nor was df overwritten). When you next call the gather() function using df as the first argument, it is using the original object passed to the tidyfy_transect_data() function.

In the second function, you pass the result of the names() function (a character vector) as the first argument to gather(), rather than an expected whole data frame. I think that’s where your “no applicable method of gather applied to type character” comes from.

If I’m understanding your goal properly, you can take advantage of additional arguments in the gather() function to exclude columns from the gather operation that you want to remain tethered to all of the key-value pairs in its row. Use the minus sign in front of bare column names (or a vector of column names created using the c() function) to copy the value from those columns into the new rows generated by gathering the wide-form data.

Does this get you what you are looking for?

###

transect.binary.2016 <- read.csv("transect_binary_2016_sample.csv")

t_transect.binary.2016 <-
  transect.binary.2016 %>%
  select(-X) %>%  # Here I dropped the X column, which was read in by the read.csv() function and appears to be the row names from your data sample
  gather(key = "veg.species", 
         value = "veg.present", 
         -c(year, 
            plot.code, 
            soil, 
            ttl.spp, 
            plot.number, 
            plot.ID, 
            total.shrub.max, 
            bare.ground.plot, 
            litter.cover.plot, 
            rock.plot, 
            total.shrub.plot, 
            litter.depth.plot))

###

Mike

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: first attempts with tidyverse and pipes
parts:
In addition to the very good advice you've already received, let me
add a trivial footnote. I think your original instinct that something
useful ought to come out at the end of a pipeline is valid, but that's
not how R implements things.

OTOH, you *can* employ the oft-neglected right-assignment arrow to
some benefit in pipelines. See the appended for a tiny example.

-- Mike


library(dplyr)

mtcars %>%
select(mpg, disp) %>%
filter(mpg > mean(mpg)) -> frugal_cars

print(frugal_cars)
